vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: extract-memories
Version: 3.0.4

The 'extract-memories' skill is designed to automate the summarization and storage of conversation highlights into a structured local directory (memory/topics/). While it requests broad permissions such as FileWrite and sessions_history, these are strictly aligned with its stated purpose of maintaining a long-term memory index (MEMORY.md). No indicators of data exfiltration, unauthorized command execution, or malicious prompt injection were found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior (reading session history and persistently writing extracted conversation 'memories' to disk) is coherent with its description, but the runtime instructions lack safeguards for sensitive data, consent, and redaction—so proceed with caution.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill extracts conversation content into topic files under memory/topics/ and updates MEMORY.md. Required capabilities (reading conversation, reading/writing memory files) are appropriate for that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to read the main session history and conversation context (sessions_history) and write persistent files (append mode) into memory/topics/ and MEMORY.md. There are no runtime safeguards described for redacting secrets, obtaining explicit user consent, or validating what gets persisted beyond a textual 'What NOT to Save' guideline. This creates a real risk of unintentionally storing sensitive information (passwords, tokens, private PII). The skill also recommends automatic invocation on conversation end and heartbeat-based triggers, which increases the chance of automatic, unreviewed persistence.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — lowest install risk. Nothing is downloaded or executed from external sources.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry declares no environment variables or external credentials (appropriate). However, the SKILL.md requests file read/write and sessions_history access (permissions, not env vars). Those permissions are proportional to the stated function but are privacy-sensitive because they allow long-term storage of conversation data. No other unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The skill writes persistent files within the agent's memory directory, which is expected for a memory-extraction tool. Autonomous invocation is allowed (disable-model-invocation:false) and the SKILL.md explicitly promotes automatic triggers — combine that with file-write permissions and you get persistent writes that may occur without explicit per-session confirmation. The skill does not request modification of other skills or global agent configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (extract conversation summaries into memory files), but it will read conversation history and write persistent files. Before installing, consider: 1) Do you want the agent to store conversation content persistently? 2) Where are memory/ files stored and who can access them? 3) Add explicit consent and redaction rules (PII, secrets, credentials) before automatic extraction. 4) Prefer manual triggers (disable automatic heartbeat/auto-extract) until you audit outputs. 5) Test in a sandbox account and inspect memory/topics/ and MEMORY.md for sensitive content. 6) If you proceed, implement retention/cleanup policies and restrict filesystem permissions for the memory directory.
